newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: ASEAN officials raise no objections on Burma.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN officials raise no objections on Burma.

text.p: Burma's proposed entry into the Association of Southeast Asian Nations was discussed by senior ASEAN officials at a meeting on Friday and no member raised any objections, Malaysia's representative said.

Malaysia's Foreign Ministry Secretary-General Abdul Kadir Mohamad told reporters at the end of the two-day meeting that neither the Philippines nor any other member of the group expressed any reservations.

Kadir stressed that no decision has been made about Burma's membership. The group noted Burma has made a formal application to join ASEAN at its annual meeting next July. Malaysia, the current ASEAN chairman, will host that meeting.

Philippine President Fidel Ramos said earlier this month that ASEAN might review its policy of "constructive engagement" with Rangoon after the military junta renewed a crackdown on a pro-democracy movement led by Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.

ASEAN -- grouping Malaysia, Indonesia, Brunei, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam -- argues that it is better to keep Burma engaged in forums like ASEAN and reform it from within than allow it to drift into isolation.
"In this meeting we did not hear that kind of reservation as we heard in the press," Kadir said, referring to the statement by Ramos.
Kadir said the question of Burma's membership would be discussed at a meeting of ASEAN foreign ministers in Manila on November 20, ahead of the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
The Burma issue would also be discussed at an informal summit of ASEAN leaders in Jakarta on November 30.
